submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as the optimal choice for the RICH detector. While Radiator-R2 achieves the best pion/kaon separation performance (4.761σ at 3 cm), it fails the critical lifetime constraint due to hygroscopic degradation risk (hygroscopic NaF crystals without hydrophobic protection). Radiator-R1 provides excellent separation (3.948σ at 3 cm) - only 17.1% lower than R2 - while ensuring reliable performance over the experiment's lifetime with its hydrophobic protective coating. This represents a 36% improvement over Radiator-R3 (2.892σ), making it substantially better than the lowest-performing option. The 3 cm thickness optimizes the balance between photon yield and chromatic effects, maximizing the separation power within the allowed 1-6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R1 achieves 3.948σ separation at optimal thickness, providing excellent particle identification. While R2 performs better (4.761σ), R1 offers the best separation among radiators that meet all constraints.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is one of the three candidates evaluated (R1, R2, R3).

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: R1 passes lifetime constraint (R1_passes_lifetime_constraint = 1) with low risk level (R1_lifetime_risk_level = 1) due to hydrophobic protection (R1_has_hydrophobic_protection = 1). R2 fails this constraint (R2_passes_lifetime_constraint = 0) with high risk (R2_lifetime_risk_level = 3).
Recommended thickness of 3 cm falls within the allowed range of 1-6 cm.
